implementation_notes: Go has no proxy class; the idiom is a function that takes the next http.Handler and returns a handler that verifies the request and then delegates, so gates nest by wrapping (edge(inner(resource))) and the nesting order is the check order. What replaces the classic structure: the net/http Handler interface plus function wrapping replaces the proxy object and the hand-built chain, and request-scoped identity travels in the request's context, set by the gate that verified it; the classic structure is still justified when the guarded surface is not net/http (a gRPC interceptor chain) or when a gate must wrap the ResponseWriter to observe what the inner handler wrote.
pitfalls: A context value is only as trustworthy as the gate that stored it; a later gate must re-verify instead of reading the stored identity as proof.
Wrapping the ResponseWriter to inspect inner handlers silently drops Flush, Hijack and Pusher interfaces, which breaks streaming and protocol upgrades behind the gate.
A handler registered directly on the mux, or a second listener, bypasses the wrapper chain; register routes so that wrapping is the only way in.
